front:
## Bias vs Variance Tradeoff

What is underfitting and overfitting?
back:
**Bias** — error from wrong assumptions. High bias → **underfitting** (model too simple).

**Variance** — error from sensitivity to training noise. High variance → **overfitting** (model too complex).

| | High Bias | High Variance |
|---|---|---|
| Train error | High | Low |
| Test error | High | High |
| Fix | More complex model | Regularisation, more data |

> Optimal models balance bias and variance — often visualised as a U-curve for test error vs model complexity.

front: ## What is regularisation? Compare L1 and L2.
back:
**Regularisation** — adds a penalty term to the loss function to discourage overly large weights.

| | L1 (Lasso) | L2 (Ridge) |
|---|---|---|
| Penalty | `λ Σ|wᵢ|` | `λ Σwᵢ²` |
| Effect | Sparse weights (some = 0) | Small weights (none exactly 0) |
| Feature selection | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Convex | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |

> L1 is preferred when you suspect many features are irrelevant. L2 works better when most features contribute.
